title: kv-cache: memory management improvements and adaptive eviction/defrag heuristics to reduce fragmentation and spillover
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We continue to see production KV cache memory fragmentation that leads to unexpected spillover to host memory under high-concurrency workloads and long-tail sequences. This PR implements an adaptive memory management pipeline that reduces fragmentation, improves compaction/defragmentation scheduling, and prioritizes spillover eviction to minimize tail latency and OOMs.

Summary of changes: 1) Introduce an in-place incremental compaction pass that runs concurrently with inference kernels; compaction is cooperative (yields to inference) and bounded by a per-shard budget to avoid CPU interference. 2) Add an adaptive eviction policy which combines LRU with sequence-length weighting and reference-frequency to prefer evicting large, cold KV blocks before spilling hot/prefix entries. 3) Implement a two-tier spillover: hot prefix pages are moved to local NVMe-backed spill files with async prefetch; cold pages are paged to host memory. 4) New fragmentation-aware allocator: bins allocations by block-size class and tracks internal fragmentation to trigger compaction when fragmentation ratio exceeds a threshold. 5) Scheduler improvements: background maintenance tasks are scheduled on a low-priority worker pool and integrated with the continuous batching scheduler so that maintenance work is throttled when latency SLOs are near threshold. 6) Expose tunables via config flags (kv.compaction.enabled, kv.compaction.budget_ms, kv.eviction.rate_limit, kv.spill.nvme_path, kv.fragmentation.threshold). 7) Add tracing/metrics: kv.fragmentation_ratio, kv.compaction_runs, kv.prefetch_hits, kv.spill_io_latency to help ops tune settings. 8) Add unit and integration tests and a perf-canary harness to exercise worst-case fragmentation workloads.

Why this approach: Prior attempts to eagerly compact or to purely LRU-evict introduced CPU contention or regressed latency under bursty traffic. The cooperative, budgeted compaction plus fragmentation-aware allocator reduces the need for aggressive background work, while the weighted-eviction policy reduces tail latencies by preserving hot prefixes in GPU memory. NVMe-backed spill for hot-but-infrequent pages reduces synchronous host-page faults and speeds up recovery.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear ENG-1427 - [x] Unit tests for allocator and eviction logic - [x] Integration tests with continuous batching enabled - [x] Perf canary results included - [x] Docs/console flags and default values updated - [x] Feature gated behind kv.compaction.enabled=false by default in main (opt-in)

Testing and results: Ran the perf-canary workload (high-concurrency, mixed sequence lengths) comparing main@HEAD vs this branch. Key results: - 98th percentile generation tail latency reduced by ~18% under 1000-concurrency mixed seq workload. - OOM incidents on a maintained canary fleet dropped from 6/week -> 0 during test window. - Average additional CPU utilization for compaction workers: +3% (configurable by budget). - End-to-end token throughput unchanged within measurement noise.

Risks and rollout plan: Feature is opt-in by default. Plan to enable kv.compaction.enabled=true in a small canary cohort (10 nodes) for 48h, monitor kv.fragmentation_ratio and tail latency, then gradually roll out. If we observe CPU-pressure regressions, reduce kv.compaction.budget_ms or disable compaction.

Related: ENG-1427 (design), ENG-1589 (scheduler integration), SUP-3112 (customer-reported OOM incidents during long conversation sessions).

feat(kv): implement cooperative incremental compaction background worker
perf(kv): weighted eviction combining LRU and sequence-length heuristics

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Overall LGTM. A couple of nits: 1) please document the failure modes when the NVMe device becomes saturated and 2) can you add a metric for compaction backlog size?
Maya Chen (author reply): Added the NVMe saturation section to docs/ops/kv_cache_tuning.md and added kv.compaction.backlog metric. Thanks for the catch.
Lina Torres: We saw a small regression in one unit test when running with ASAN enabled; looks like a race during compaction shutdown. Please add a graceful stop path for compaction worker.
Maya Chen (author reply): Fixed shutdown race by adding a drain-and-stop handshake; added a regression test. Verified under ASAN locally.
Samir Gupta: Suggest we run the perf-canary for 48h on canary fleet before merging; also please ensure the default in main remains disabled.
Maya Chen (author reply): Agreed on the canary. Branch keeps kv.compaction.enabled=false by default; will schedule 48h canary after merge for opt-in rollout.
Ops comment (internal): SUP-3112 customer asked for faster NVMe prefetch; lowered prefetch window introduced small extra IO but improved latency - documented tradeoffs.
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory management: introduces fragmentation-aware allocator, cooperative compaction, weighted eviction, and NVMe-backed spill with async prefetch. Opt-in behind kv.compaction.enabled=false by default. Expected to reduce OOMs and tail latency in high-fragmentation workloads.
notes_for_oncall: If customers report increased CPU usage after enabling compaction, reduce kv.compaction.budget_ms or set kv.compaction.enabled=false. Watch kv.fragmentation_ratio, kv.compaction_runs and kv.spill_io_latency. If NVMe device IO saturation occurs, set kv.spill.nvme_path to a larger device or fall back to host paging.
perf_results_summary: 98th pctl tail latency -18% on mixed seq workload; OOMs in canary fleet: reduced from 6/week to 0 in test window; compaction CPU overhead +3%.
